references.text: Basic instructions for the grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, which is the same type of offering mentioned in Leviticus 23:13.
Describes the grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Specifies the amount of the grain offering (one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil) and the drink offering (one-fourth of a hin of wine) that must accompany the burnt offering.
Indicates two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as the grain offering, corresponding to the amount in Leviticus 23:13.
Describes the grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil and the drink offering of wine as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Early instruction regarding the grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil and the drink offering of wine as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
First mention of 'pleasing aroma' (ריח ניחח) in the Bible, using the same expression found in Leviticus 23:13.
Describes the burnt offering as a fire offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord (אשה ריח ניחח ליהוה).
Ezekiel's vision of the future temple includes grain offerings of fine flour and oil.
